chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi, from Ali ibn al-Mu'alla, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn al-Subbah, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, the companion of al-Sabiri al-Bajali, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever is killed defending his dependents, he is a martyr.'

key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ: Peace be upon him and his family

ai.seo_question: Who is considered a martyr if they die defending their family?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on fighting the *Muhibith* (warrior/brigand), this hadith expands the definition of martyrdom beyond battlefield death to include those killed while defending their dependents (*ayal*). This ruling underscores the high spiritual status of familial protection in Shia jurisprudence, linking the preservation of one's lineage directly to the reward of martyrdom.
